grounded.context: in cells expressing mutant RPA32 or DNA-PKcs
grounded.evidence_quote: Cells expressing mutant RPA32 or DNA-PKcs show sustained H2AX phosphorylation in response to replication stress that persists in cells entering mitosis, indicating inappropriate mitotic entry with unrepaired damage.
Replication stress activates ATR, which phosphorylates/activates Chk1, and this is a key step in transmitting DNA damage signals to downstream replication checkpoint effector proteins (52,55).
